# Command reference

Every command of cmdAbl, generated from the declarations the platform itself parses, resolves and
shows as help. Type a command in the palette; `<command> --help` prints the same information.

## `arm`

toggle record arm on tracks

Switches record arm on for each track that is not armed and off for each that is, one by one. With --set 1 every track ends up armed, with --set 0 not armed, whatever it was before; a track that is already in that state counts as done. Return, main and group tracks cannot be armed and are reported as failed (disarming them is a no-op). With the cmdAbl Remote Script running, tracks Live refuses to arm (for example a MIDI track whose input device is not available) are reported as failed too. Live's Exclusive Arm setting is not applied: naming several tracks arms all of them.

**Usage:** `arm [--set <0|1>] <track>…`

| Argument | Kind | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<track>…` | path (track) | yes | Tracks to arm; separate several with commas |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-s, --set <0|1>` | make sure every target is armed (1) or not (0) instead of toggling |

**Examples**

```
arm /Bass
```

arm or disarm the track Bass

```
arm /Bass, /Lead
```

several tracks, separated by a comma

```
arm --set 1 /Bass
```

make sure Bass is armed

```
arm --set 0 /Bass, /Lead
```

disarm both

## `cmdabl`

configure cmdAbl

Setup and status commands of cmdAbl itself.

**Usage:** `cmdabl <command>`

**Subcommands:** `setup`, `bridge`

### `cmdabl setup`

install trigger and Remote Script, then say what to do next

Installs the keyboard trigger (Karabiner on macOS, AutoHotkey on Windows) and copies the Remote Script into Live's User Library, then compares the shipped, installed and running script versions and says what to do: restart Live, enable the control surface, or nothing.

**Usage:** `cmdabl setup`

**Examples**

```
cmdabl setup
```

run once after installing, and again after updating cmdAbl

### `cmdabl bridge`

show the Remote Script status (version, response time)

Sends one fresh request to the Remote Script and reports its version, protocol, response time and operations.

**Usage:** `cmdabl bridge`

**Examples**

```
cmdabl bridge
```

check that the Remote Script is installed and running

## `find`

find tracks, devices and chains whose path contains a pattern

Looks through the Live Set for tracks, devices, rack chains and Drum Rack pads whose path contains every word of the pattern, in any order and ignoring case. One match is selected; several are shown in a pick list. next and prev then step through the matches. Needs the cmdAbl Remote Script. find remembers its last list until the extension restarts.

**Usage:** `find [--tracks] [--devices] [--chains] [--unfold] <pattern>`

| Argument | Kind | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<pattern>` | text | yes | Words that must all occur in the path, in any order (takes the rest of the line) |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-t, --tracks` | only tracks |
| `-d, --devices` | only devices |
| `-c, --chains` | only chains and drum pads |
| `--unfold` | also show the track's chains in the Session mixer when selecting (never folds anything) |

- Needs the Remote Script (reports "not running" / "outdated" otherwise).

**Examples**

```
find kick
```

everything with "kick" in its path

```
find vermona kick
```

paths containing both words

```
find -c kick
```

only chains and drum pads

```
find -t -c kick
```

only tracks and chains

```
find --unfold kick
```

also show the track's chains in the Session mixer

## `goto`

select a track, device, chain or drum pad by path

Selects the object in Live: a track becomes the selected track; a device, chain or pad is selected in its track's device chain. Needs the cmdAbl Remote Script. Picking an object in the palette runs this command for you. When your words match several objects you are asked to choose one.

**Usage:** `goto [--unfold] <path>`

| Argument | Kind | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<path>` | path (any object) | yes | Path of the track, device, chain or pad; spaces need no quotes (takes the rest of the line) |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--unfold` | also show the track's chains in the Session mixer (never folds anything) |

- Needs the Remote Script (reports "not running" / "outdated" otherwise).

**Examples**

```
goto /Vermona MIDI
```

select a track

```
goto /Vermona MIDI/Drum Rack/Kick
```

select a pad inside a Drum Rack

```
goto kick
```

select the object with "kick" in its name (you choose when there are several)

```
goto --unfold /Vermona MIDI
```

select a track and show its chains in the Session mixer

## `help`

list the available commands

Prints every command with its one-line summary. Typing a command followed by --help shows that command in full.

**Usage:** `help`

**Examples**

```
help
```

list the commands

```
cmdabl --help
```

usage of the cmdabl commands

## `lom`

show the Live Object Model path of a track, device or chain

Shows the object's cmdAbl path, its Live Object Model path (the address used by Max for Live's live.path and in Remote Scripts) and the link to the LOM reference page that describes its kind. Only reads; it does not need the cmdAbl Remote Script. When your words match several objects you are asked to choose one.

**Usage:** `lom <target>`

| Argument | Kind | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<target>` | path (track / device / chain) | yes | Track, device, chain or pad; spaces need no quotes (takes the rest of the line) |

**Examples**

```
lom /Vermona MIDI
```

the LOM path of a track

```
lom /Vermona MIDI/Drum Rack/Kick
```

the LOM path of a pad inside a Drum Rack

```
lom kick
```

the object with "kick" in its name

## `man`

open a manual, or search it: ableton, cmdabl

Opens a manual in your web browser: the Ableton Live reference manual or the cmdAbl documentation. Words after ableton search the Live 12 manual through Ecosia. Needs an internet connection.

**Usage:** `man <ableton|cmdabl> [<words>]`

| Argument | Kind | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<topic>` | one of `ableton`, `cmdabl` | yes | Which manual: ableton (Live reference manual) or cmdabl (this documentation) |
| `<words>` | text | no | What to search for; only for ableton (takes the rest of the line) |

**Examples**

```
man ableton
```

open the Live reference manual

```
man ableton warp modes
```

search the Live manual for "warp modes"

```
man cmdabl
```

open the cmdAbl documentation

## `mute`

toggle mute on tracks, chains and drum pads

Switches mute on for each target that is not muted and off for each that is, one by one. With --set 1 every target ends up muted, with --set 0 unmuted, whatever it was before; a target that is already in that state counts as done. Works on tracks, rack chains and Drum Rack pads. Tracks work on their own; chains and pads need the cmdAbl Remote Script and macOS. When a word matches several objects you are asked to choose.

**Usage:** `mute [--set <0|1>] <track>…`

| Argument | Kind | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<track>…` | path (track / chain) | yes | Tracks, rack chains or Drum Rack pads; separate several with commas |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-s, --set <0|1>` | make sure every target is muted (1) or not (0) instead of toggling |

**Examples**

```
mute /Kick
```

mute or unmute the track Kick

```
mute /Kick, /Snare
```

several targets, separated by a comma

```
mute --set 1 /Kick, /Snare
```

make sure both are muted

```
mute --set 0 /Kick
```

make sure Kick is not muted

```
mute vermona kick
```

words that all occur in one path; if each word also names something on its own, you are asked which you mean

## `next`

go to the next match of the last find

Selects the next object of the last find (or of the last pick list), wrapping around at the end. Keeps the find's --unfold choice (a list from another pick steps without it). Needs the cmdAbl Remote Script. Without an earlier find there is nothing to step through.

**Usage:** `next`

- Needs the Remote Script (reports "not running" / "outdated" otherwise).

**Examples**

```
next
```

go to the next match of the last find

## `pakabl`

install and manage Ableton Live extensions

Installs and manages community extensions for Ableton Live (.ablx files) from cmdAbl's curated list of community repositories. Run pakabl update once to fetch the list, then pakabl list to browse it. Restart Live after installing, upgrading or removing an extension.

**Usage:** `pakabl <command>`

**Subcommands:** `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `upgrade`, `list`

### `pakabl install`

download and install an extension from the curated index

Downloads one Ableton Live extension from the curated list and unpacks it into Live's Extensions folder. Restart Live to load it. Run pakabl update first to fetch the list.

**Usage:** `pakabl install <id>`

| Argument | Kind | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<id>` | text | yes | Extension id as shown by pakabl list: author.name |

**Examples**

```
pakabl install federico-pepe.snake
```

install the extension with that id

### `pakabl uninstall`

remove an installed extension

Deletes an installed extension from Live's Extensions folder. Restart Live to unload it.

**Usage:** `pakabl uninstall <id>`

| Argument | Kind | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<id>` | text | yes | Extension id as shown by pakabl list: author.name |

- Removes or irreversibly changes something; takes one target per address, never every match.

**Examples**

```
pakabl uninstall federico-pepe.snake
```

remove that extension

### `pakabl update`

refresh the curated index

Fetches the current curated list of extensions. Needed once before install, upgrade and list, and again whenever you want to see new versions.

**Usage:** `pakabl update`

**Examples**

```
pakabl update
```

fetch the list

### `pakabl upgrade`

install the index's version of an extension (&lt;id>@&lt;version> checks the version)

Installs the version the curated list holds, replacing an installed one. Name the version you expect after an @ and the command stops when the list has another one. Restart Live to reload it.

**Usage:** `pakabl upgrade <ref>`

| Argument | Kind | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<ref>` | text | yes | Extension id, optionally followed by @ and the version you expect |

**Examples**

```
pakabl upgrade federico-pepe.snake
```

install the list's version

```
pakabl upgrade federico-pepe.snake@1.2.0
```

only if the list holds version 1.2.0

### `pakabl list`

browse the curated extensions and install or remove them

Opens a window with the curated extensions. Each row has buttons to install, update or uninstall it and to open its repository. Run pakabl update first to fetch the list.

**Usage:** `pakabl list`

**Examples**

```
pakabl list
```

browse the extensions

## `prev`

go to the previous match of the last find

Selects the previous object of the last find (or of the last pick list), wrapping around at the start. Keeps the find's --unfold choice (a list from another pick steps without it). Needs the cmdAbl Remote Script. Without an earlier find there is nothing to step through.

**Usage:** `prev`

- Needs the Remote Script (reports "not running" / "outdated" otherwise).

**Examples**

```
prev
```

go to the previous match of the last find

## `solo`

toggle solo on tracks, chains and drum pads

Switches solo on for each target that is not soloed and off for each that is, one by one. With --set 1 every target ends up soloed, with --set 0 not soloed, whatever it was before; a target that is already in that state counts as done. Works on tracks, rack chains and Drum Rack pads. Tracks work on their own; chains and pads need the cmdAbl Remote Script and macOS. Live's Exclusive Solo setting is not applied: naming several targets solos all of them.

**Usage:** `solo [--set <0|1>] <track>…`

| Argument | Kind | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<track>…` | path (track / chain) | yes | Tracks, rack chains or Drum Rack pads; separate several with commas |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-s, --set <0|1>` | make sure every target is soloed (1) or not (0) instead of toggling |

**Examples**

```
solo /Kick
```

solo or unsolo the track Kick

```
solo /Kick, /Snare
```

several targets, separated by a comma

```
solo --set 1 /Kick
```

make sure Kick is soloed

```
solo --set 0 /Kick, /Snare
```

make sure neither is soloed

```
solo vermona kick
```

words that all occur in one path; if each word also names something on its own, you are asked which you mean

## `tree`

list the tracks, devices and chains of the Live Set as a tree

Lists the Live Set as an indented tree: tracks (regular, return, main), their devices, and the chains and drum pads of racks, each with its kind, and a last line counting what is listed. Without a path it starts at the whole Set; with a path it starts at that track, device or chain. -L sets how many levels below the start are shown (default 2). Only reads; chains and pads appear when the cmdAbl Remote Script is running. A listing of more than 200 lines is cut: pass a path or a smaller -L.

**Usage:** `tree [--level <n>] [<path>]`

| Argument | Kind | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<path>` | path (track / device / chain) | no | Where the listing starts: a track, device or chain; without it, the whole Set (takes the rest of the line) |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-L, --level <n>` | how many levels below the start are shown (default 2) (a whole number from 1 to 12) |

**Examples**

```
tree
```

the whole Set, two levels: tracks and their devices

```
tree /Vermona MIDI
```

one track with its devices and chains

```
tree -L 3 vermona
```

three levels below the object matching "vermona"

```
tree --level 1
```

only the tracks
